  Paycom sells a cloud-based, single-database Human Capital Management

  small/mid-market employers. Its differentiation is that the employee
  does the data entry (self-service "Beti"), reducing client HR workload
  and creating a database lock-in that makes switching to ADP/UKG a
  re-implementation project. It monetizes via per-employee-per-month
  fees with high incremental margins once the base is built.
  Understandability: HIGH.

  • Switching costs: 3 — payroll records, benefits administration,
    employee-training lock-in; very high in practice
  • Network effects: 1 — limited (client data silos, not cross-client)
  • Cost advantage: 2 — integrated single-database lowers support costs
    vs multi-vendor installs
  • Economies of scale: 2 — scale present but smaller than ADP/PAYX
  • Regulatory barriers: 1 — tax/compliance complexity helps incumbents,
    but not a license barrier
  • Data moat: 2 — proprietary payroll/employee data accumulates, but

  Positive: The 20% buyback at higher prices strengthens EPS optics and
  attracts momentum inflows; SBC dilution is partly offset; talent
  attraction improves with a higher stock.
  Negative: A sharp de-rating (e.g., recession, hike → 10Y to 5.5%)
  would expose the leverage ($900M floating) and hurt confidence in
  the buyback — a reflexive spiral. Probability of material down-reflex:
  15-20% [Estimate].

Step 3.5-3. Customer Behavior
  Paycom's SMB base is mid-market (100-1,000 employees); as the product
  automates, CAC/implementation churn may rise for very small clients
  (DIY trend). LTV/CAC may compress at low end, but retention at
  mid-market stays. Forecast keeps growth in high-single digits.
